body:
The solution for this is going to involve adding relevant code to ensure that particle shaders/pipelines are compiled during background resource loading. Basically, some of the ubershader scaffolding will need to be added. Fortunately though, what makes the ubershaders complicated is the need to handle many different vertex formats, framebuffer formats, etc. and particles, being compute shaders, don't have any of that. 

That is why particles pipelines can queue up pipeline creation as soon as the shader code is set.

It looks like the problem here is mostly coming from stalling while waiting for the _shader_ to compile.  The stall is happening because the shader compilation goes wide, and then immediately needs to be waited on so the shader can be used to compile the pipelines. 

**Workaround**

As discussed on RC. A workaround for this is to simply compile fewer Particles shaders. To do that, you can modify ParticlesProcessMaterial to remove the variants that you don't need, and then collapse all the other branches into uniform branches that are set with uniform bools. This will increase the GPU run time cost of your particle shaders marginally, but can result in having very few shaders that need to compile

**Solution**

The solution is going to involve a few things:
1. Avoid waiting on the shader compilation immediately after it starts
2. Either delay compiling the pipelines, or bundle the shader checks onto the background thread (or both)
3. Avoid waiting on the shader in the higher level code. 

A lot of refactoring went into BaseMaterial to allow it to be used without forcing a stall on compiling the shaders. Particularly important is `material_create_from_shader()`. You can see how it is used in BaseMaterial:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d0a589777829c2c3fdf5ce64964afbed57e7794/scene/resources/material.cpp#L2089-L2104

Importantly, this allows you to defer calling `material_set_shader()` until something requests the RID of the material. Once that happens, you create the material and assign the shader in one go. 

Note how `material_set_shader()` is called right after the shader is created (which calls `shader_set_code()`)

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d0a589777829c2c3fdf5ce64964afbed57e7794/scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp#L1222-L1223

While in BaseMaterial, you can skip it and it will get called as part of `material_create_from_shader()` when the RID of the material is actually needed (which typically doesn't happen until run time):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d0a589777829c2c3fdf5ce64964afbed57e7794/scene/resources/material.cpp#L2084-L2086
I'm running into this, too - significant lag at every first particle instantiation on Godot 4.6 with D3D12.
